newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold to drift, silver, platinum seen up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold to drift, silver, platinum seen up.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold is expected to drift lower on Monday and could tumble towards $321.00 an ounce if initial support at $324.00 is breached, traders and chartwatchers said.
Silver is expected to consolidate before mounting another attack of $4.55, while platinum has the potential to move towards $450.00 if it can overcome resistance above $440.00,, they added.
GOLD - Looks set to drift towards $321.00 an ounce if the market breaks below $324.00.

In early Monday European trading gold was straddling this level following Australian and Japanese trader selling. "It's under pressure but if $324.00 holds then the market should enter into consolidation," one trader commented.
Buoyant silver and platinum markets may lend some support to silver, traders said.
"The technical indicators are drifting sideways as the metal looks for direction," Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said.
Referring to the December gold Comex contract, Squires said, "We look for initial weakness to show to test support at $326.60, then $325.10."
On the upside gold is expected to find resistance just above $325.00, followed by a stiff band between $328/$329.
At 0800 GMT spot gold was quoted at $323.80/$324.20, versus Friday's London close of $324.00/$324.50s close.

SILVER - May attempt to fill a chart gap on the charts between $4.50 and $4.55, traders said on Monday. The recent move above stiff resistance at $4.40 continues to bolster upside sentiment. "The market is looking for higher levels," a trader said.
A breach of $4.55 could spark a move to $4.80 and $4.90.
At 0800 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.46/4.48, versus $4.44/$4.46.

PLATINUM - A tight physical market and a rampaging palladium market is likely to spark gains in platinum. On Monday yen-based palladium futures contracts on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange surged to their daily limit, a move that prompted gains in platinum.
Traders said tight supplies despite the resumption of Russian shipments should continue to under the market.
Russian shipments of PGMs resumed in July after a six month suspension but the market continues to reflect the tightness left by Russia being out of the market since last December.
Traders said the market is eyeing the July 12 high of $452.00.
At 0800 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $440.00/443.00 against $4.37/$440.00. Palladium was indicated at $227.00/$237.00 compared with $223.00/$228.00. --London Newsroom +44 171 542-8075
